The lesion was painless and progressive in nature and did not obstruct the vision of the patient. The best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was recorded to be 6/6 for both eyes. The lesion involving the left side of the forehead and face, on examination, appeared to be a typical sebaceous nevus. These lesions were linearly arranged, slightly elevated, hyperpigmented plaques (Figure 2).

in_text_mentions: Our patient was an Asian girl who was delivered at 36 weeks of gestation with normal antenatal screening. Her family history was unremarkable. Newborn examination revealed multiple well-defined yellowish plaques over her body, involving her scalp, face, neck, right chest, and upper limb (Figure 1a). Ophthalmological examination showed chorioretinal coloboma in her right eye and a lipodermoid at her left upper eyelid (Figure 1b). She was diagnosed with linear nevus sebaceous syndrome.

Caption states acanthosis, papillomatosis, mild hyperkeratosis; in-text states proliferation of sebaceous glands and primitive hair follicles indicating nevus sebaceous, supporting sebaceous gland hyperplasia histology finding.
panels.attribution_text: Pandya et al. Linear Nevus Sebaceous Syndrome: Clinical Presentation and Management Considerations.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.60487. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 6.
panels.figure_caption: The sections from the provided tissue specimen show acanthosis, papillomatosis, and mild hyperkeratosis
in_text_mentions: ng Ethilon 3-0 and Vicryl 3-0. Subsequently, the excised tissue was sent for histopathological examination. A single cutaneous tissue specimen, with skin attached, measuring 20 x 6 x 0.2 cm, was provided for histopathological evaluation. The sections of the provided tissue specimen show acanthosis, papillomatosis, and mild hyperkeratosis. The histopathology reveals a focal absence of the granular layer underlying the dermis, with extensive areas of proliferation of sebaceous glands and primitive hair follicles. The histopathological features indicate the presence of nevus sebaceous (Figure 6).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Lateral head photo of the reported Schimmelpenning syndrome patient showing dense verrucous brown plaques over the scalp and face; matches captioned epidermal nevi of the configured disease. B: Frontal view of the same patient showing multicolored verrucous nevi on the face and upper chest, a classic cutaneous manifestation of nevus sebaceous syndrome. C: Trunk photograph showing extensive left-predominant multicolored epidermal nevi, explicitly captioned for this Schimmelpenning syndrome patient. D: Anterior lower-limb photo showing linear verrucous nevus lesions consistent with the captioned diffuse epidermal nevi of the same patient. E: Posterior leg view demonstrating extensive linear verrucous nevi matching the captioned manifestations of Schimmelpenning (nevus sebaceous) syndrome.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels ((a), (b), (c), (d)). (a): The panel shows MRA evidence of narrowing in the distal aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta, which is discussed in the context of a case of Nevus Sebaceous Syndrome. (b): The panel displays MRA evidence of narrowing at the abdominal aorta, presented within the clinical context of Nevus Sebaceous Syndrome. (c): The panel shows MRA evidence of bilateral renal artery stenoses, which is linked to the case presentation of Nevus Sebaceous Syndrome. (d): The panel shows MRA evidence of a right cystic kidney, noted in the context of the patient's Nevus Sebaceous Syndrome presentation.

panels.figure_caption: Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) showed (a) narrowing at the distal aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta, (b) narrowing at the abdominal aorta, (c) bilateral renal artery stenoses, and (d) right cystic kidney.
in_text_mentions: Magnetic resonance angiogram revealed diffuse aortopathy involving the aortic arch (5 mm in diameter at isthmus), thoracic aorta (7 mm), and abdominal aorta (5 mm). The main branches from the aorta were also affected, including bilateral renal artery stenoses (RAS) and narrowed celiac trunk and superior mesenteric artery (2–3 mm in diameter) (Figure 3). The Doppler ultrasound did not show focal stenosis in her common, internal, or external carotid arteries.
